content:
rosie: hey all — day 2 here, trying to build the runtime from source and hitting a linker error. I followed the README but I'm stuck. :wave:

rosie: build command I'm running:
```
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 ..
cmake --build build -j16
```

rosie: error output (tail):
```
[100%] Linking CXX executable redwood-runtime
/usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `cublasLtMatmul'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

rosie: `nvcc --version` shows CUDA 12.1, but `nvidia-smi` reports Driver Version: 525.85.12. Not sure if that's the problem. who should I ping for driver/toolkit mismatch advice?

sam: hi @rosie, welcome! for linker errors like that usually it's either missing -lcublasLt or the runtime is picking up headers from one toolkit and libs from another. quick checks: is /usr/local/cuda a symlink to cuda-12.1? run `ls -l /usr/local/cuda` and `ldconfig -p | grep cublas`.

miguel: also check that your LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes the cuda lib64 path during link time (and for runtime): `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. some distros drop /usr/local/cuda from the default search.

rosie: thanks. output:
```
$ ls -l /usr/local/cuda
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 15 Mar  5 12:00 /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8

$ nvcc --version
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105
```

rosie: so the symlink points to 11.8 but nvcc reports 12.1. I probably have mixed installs.

paige: ah that explains it. the binary build was using headers from 12.1 but the runtime linker finds 11.8 libs. two options: update the symlink to point to 12.1, or install the matching driver/lib for 11.8. we prefer pointing /usr/local/cuda -> cuda-12.1 for dev machines unless you're deliberately using older runtime.

miguel: if you don't want to change system symlinks, you can pass explicit flags to cmake: `-DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 -DCUDA_CUDA_LIBRARY=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` and set `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64"`. but updating the symlink is simpler for most folks.

rosie: trying update symlink now (sudo). will report back.

devops-bot: deploy-checklist: please avoid changing /usr/local/cuda on corp build agents; only change on your dev VM. If you need a separate build environment, we have docker images `redwood/dev-runtime:cuda-12.1` — see https://intranet.redwood/dev-images.

rosie: fyi I'm on a personal cloud VM, safe to change. updated symlink and re-ran cmake: now the link step progresses further but I hit a new error:
```
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcublasLt_static
```

sam: that one means the static archive isn't present in the lib dir. some CUDA installs ship only shared libs. check `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` for `libcublasLt.so` vs `libcublasLt.a`. our build can link shared; check CMakeLists reference. search for `cublasLt_static` and switch to `cublasLt` if needed.

rosie: grep shows `target_link_libraries(runtime PUBLIC cublasLt_static)` in third_party/CMakeLists.txt. should I change to `cublasLt`?

miguel: yeah replace with `cublasLt` and re-run, or modify the find_package logic so it resolves shared libs. open a small patch and push to a feature branch, tag me and @sam and I'll review quickly — good onboarding PR.

rosie: ok made branch `rosie/fix-cublaslt-link` and changed to `cublasLt`. pushed — link: https://git.redwood/rosie/fix-cublaslt-link

sam: pulled and ran CI locally on my laptop container (uses cuda-12.1 image) — build passes now. nice catch.

paige: one more note: if you ever hit runtime failures on infra, check driver vs toolkit matrix here: https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/cuda-compatibility/index.html . we maintain a short cheat sheet in the onboarding docs too.

rosie: thanks everyone! will clean up the commit message and request a merge. big help. :tada:

sam: welcome aboard — ping here if you hit other weird linker/device issues. the runtime team tends to see lots of subtle ABI problems early on :)

rosie: will do, and happy to pair on the next steps for getting a dev docker image set up for me.

devops-bot: reminder: created ephemeral dev container for rosie at `dev-container-rosie-42` (expires in 7 days).
